flags.headline: US-Iran war escalates sharply over the weekend — 2 US troop deaths, 8th consecutive night of US strikes, oil above $82/bbl; markets have not yet priced this in
flags.detail: Two US service members were killed (one still missing) in an Iranian attack on a US base in Jordan on Friday 07-17; the US has continued strikes on Iran for an 8th consecutive night as of 07-19, with explosions reported in Bandar Abbas and Qeshm Island and air-raid sirens sounding in Bahrain. The ceasefire/MoU reached last month is described as 'in tatters.' Crude oil has risen to above $82/barrel (highest in a month, +10%+ on the week) on Strait of Hormuz disruption concerns; a 60-day sanctions waiver on Iranian oil sales was revoked, with transactions barred after 07-17. This is a portfolio-wide macro development, not a single-name thesis break: it is a near-term tailwind for the energy sleeve (VLO, CVX, OKE, DVN, CNX — 5 of 52 holdings) via crude/crack-spread strength, and a headwind for broader risk sentiment (rate-sensitive and high-multiple growth names) heading into Monday's open, given equities have had zero opportunity to price in two additional nights of escalation since Friday's close.
flags.thesis_link: No single held name's enumerated key_risk names this specific war-escalation path, though it bears on CVX's key_risk #1 (Brent-price sensitivity of the dividend, currently a tailwind not a threat) and is the same Iran-tension theme already noted driving VLO's crack-spread rally on 07-18. Flagged at portfolio level given the scale of the escalation (US combat deaths) and the two-session pricing gap.
